chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us. He said: Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i narrated to us from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him). He said:
One of my forefathers (peace be upon them) heard a man reciting Umm al-Quran (al-Fatiha), so he said: 'Thanksgiving and reward.'
Then he heard him reciting 'Say: He is God, the One' (al-Ikhlas), so he said: 'He has believed and is secure.'
Then he heard him reciting 'Indeed We sent it down' (al-Qadr), so he said: 'He spoke the truth, and was forgiven.'
Then he heard him reciting Ayat al-Kursi, so he said: 'Bravo, bravo! The dissociation of this person from the Fire has descended.'

key_terms.آمَنَ وَأَمِنَ: He has believed and is secure — the dual blessing of faith and safety for reciting al-Ikhlas
key_terms.آيَةُ الْكُرْسِيِّ: Ayat al-Kursi — 'the Throne Verse' (2:255), considered the greatest verse in the Quran
key_terms.أُمُّ الْقُرْآنِ: Umm al-Quran — 'the mother of the Quran,' a title for Surah al-Fatiha, indicating it is the foundation of the entire Quran
key_terms.بَرَاءَةٌ: Dissociation/freedom from the Fire — a declaration of salvation for the reciter
key_terms.شُكْرٌ وَأَجْرٌ: Thanksgiving and reward — the spiritual response to reciting al-Fatiha

ai.seo_question: What reward does an Imam promise for reciting al-Fatiha, al-Ikhlas, al-Qadr, and Ayat al-Kursi?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) narrates that one of his forefathers — an Imam from the Ahl al-Bayt — observed a man reciting four key Quranic passages and responded to each with a spiritual declaration. Each surah or verse carries a distinct blessing: al-Fatiha brings gratitude and reward, al-Ikhlas confirms faith and security, al-Qadr affirms truthfulness and forgiveness, and Ayat al-Kursi seals the reciter's freedom from hellfire. This hadith highlights the immense spiritual merit of specific Quranic recitations according to Shia tradition.
